title: Eleven Files and One Unsigned Note
subtitle: 法律与规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律与规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律与规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：detective　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 detective 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1951 the superintendent ① sent a detective that no station in the county would have spared, and he said the sending was the whole of the inquiry. The ② detective, meaning the officer and not the inquiry, ran eleven files and stayed unnamed in the report; a detective, he said, is the only thing in a station that is judged by how long he is left unsent.

Every ③ detective in that station had the same unsigned note on the desk, and the ④ detective at the end, meaning the one they kept for the river cases and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A detective, the sergeant said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to send; the superintendent said the sending is the part that fills eleven files.

The lawyer meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the detective was the whole of the case, meaning the investigation and not the officer. The ⑥ detective, meaning the investigation and not any of that, is the only thing in a case that everybody cites and nobody repeats; detective, she said, is either somebody you send or the only word that means both an officer and an investigation. She said the investigation is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ detective had become a line in a roster, and the roster had become an argument about the unsigned note. The ⑧ detective of the whole thing, the superintendent wrote in February, was one station and eleven files of sending; detective, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to send. She said the sending was never mentioned.

The ⑨ detective I remember is the one at the end, who retired in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the county. A ⑩ detective, the sergeant said in 1975, is the only one who improves by being thanked; every detective, she said, is an investigation that has agreed to look like an officer. She said the investigation was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 侦探；探员（指局里派出的那一位）
B. n. 侦探（指那位警员本人，与那次侦查相对）
C. 固定搭配：send a detective 派出一名侦探
D. n. 探员（指留给河边案子的那一位）
E. n. 侦探；探员（抽象总称，指一个警局的全部侦查）
F. n. 探员（指名册上写到、被列名的那一位）
G. n. 侦查；调查（指案子里被引述的那一次）
H. n. 侦查（抽象总称，指人人援引却无人重做的那一次）

items.q: sent a detective that no station in the county would have spared
The detective, meaning the officer and not the inquiry
the detective was the whole of the case
the detective had become a line in a roster
The detective of the whole thing
A detective, the sergeant said in 1975

answers.why: send a detective 意为“派出一名侦探”，1951 年警司派出了一位全郡没有一处警局肯割爱的侦探。
detective 意为“侦探”，指那位警员本人而不是那次侦查，他办了十一个卷宗而在报告里没有名字。
detective 意为“侦探”，指那个警局里每一位侦探，每一位的桌上都有同一张未签名的便条。
detective 意为“探员”，指留给河边案子的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
detective 意为“侦查、调查”，指案子里被引述的那一次，律师说这次侦查就是那个案子的全部。
detective 意为“侦查”，指人人援引却无人重做的那一次而不是那位警员，是案子里人人都援引、却无人重做的东西。
detective 意为“探员”，指名册上写到、被列名的那一位，到 1959 年这位侦探成了名册里的一行。
detective 意为“侦探、探员”，警司二月写道，整件事的侦查是一个警局和十一个卷宗的派出。
detective 意为“侦探”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1973 年退休，至今仍被说成全郡最安静的一位。
detective 为抽象总称，警长 1975 年说，一位侦探是唯一会因为被致谢而变得更好的人。
